London, 20<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**U.S. auto suppliers** will get as much as $5 billion in U.S. Treasury aid to avoid a collapse that would cripple the domestic industry, including federally funded General Motors Corp. and Chrysler LLC. Suppliers will get a guarantee that money owed them for products will be paid, regardless of what happens to car companies, the Treasury Department said today in a statement. The programme will be run through the automakers.  Suppliers, squeezed by production cuts at automakers, asked for $18.5 billion last month. Failure to help could mean the loss of 1 million jobs in the U.S. Lear Corp., the second- largest autoseat maker, said this month that its auditors expressed doubt about its ability to keep operating, and American Axle & Manufacturing Holdings Inc. said it may breach loan terms.   Any U.S. auto company can participate in the aid program, and GM and Chrysler have already agreed to do so, according to the Treasury statement. Ford Motor Co. doesn’t need to take part, the company said.  Suppliers will pay a fee of two percentage points for each receivable guaranteed, and an additional percentage point if the receivable is converted to cash ahead of the normal payment period of 45 to 60 days.  Not all lawmakers lauded the program. Treasury’s decision is “a violation of trust,” two U.S. Republican senators, Bob Corker of Tennessee and Judd Gregg of New Hampshire, said in a statement. Treasury had said it would use aid only for GM and Chrysler restructuring, Corker said. 

## _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**The Zagreb Transport Show** , Croatia, has been called off due to a lack of interest as a result of the global economic crisis.   Croatian sales of heavy transport vehicles plunged some 50% in the first two months of 2008 compared with the year before, and falling consumer confidence saw sales of passenger cars slump 40% over the same period after a gain of 7% in 2008. 

The British International Motor Show has been cancelled because of the crisis in the car industry. It will be the first time in peacetime the century-old event has not taken place.  The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT), the trade body which organises the two-week show in July, said it had consulted with its members before making the decision. It said it would be inappropriate to expect struggling carmakers to commit themselves to taking part. 

## _Source:  FX Street / The Guardian_ 

**Corning** has been experiencing increasing glass orders over the past several weeks at both its wholly owned business and Samsung Corning Precision Glass. Corning now believes total glass volume for the first quarter could be flat to down 5% sequentially, versus its original guidance of down 20% to 25%.  Information supplied by NPD Group, an independent consumer market research firm, shows that retail sales of LCD TVs remain strong. In the US alone, February unit sales of LCD TVs increased 39% over 2008. Si

milarly, unit sales for Japan were 30% higher year over year as indicated by data from BCN, another independent research firm. For Europe and China, only January data is available, but reports indicated year-over-year growth of 49% and 109%, respectively. As a reminder, the company is forecasting worldwide LCD TV unit sales to increase by 9% for the full year.  The company still expects significant glass price declines for the first quarter in its wholly owned business as compared to previous quarters. Corning has not reached agreements for pricing in the second quarter, but expects price declines to be more moderate than the first quarter. Market pressures could still affect these expectations.  Based on the improved volume expectations for its display business, the company now believes it will have positive net income, excluding special items, in the first quarter.
